summary.note_on_regression: The 21 new experiments in this milestone averaged 20.3 min/exp vs 14.3 min/exp for the prior 378. bottlenecks_identified: RETRO_003_STILL_OPEN — TIMEOUT_NOT_ENFORCED: The single largest bottleneck from the prior milestone (Exp 53, 418 min) persists at the top of the cumulative histogram because RETRO-003 was not closed. run_experiment_with_timeout.sh exists but the conductor does not invoke it for all experiments. Every future milestone risks a repeat 418-minute outlier until this is wired as mandatory.

RETRO_005_STILL_OPEN — ZOMBIE_RESIDUAL_VRAM: GPU state at retro time shows 4MB allocated on each RTX 3090 at 0% utilization (up from 2MB in prior retro). No active processes, but VRAM is not fully released between sessions. gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies is available but not invoked automatically between experiments. Accumulation will worsen with more sessions.

SIMULATED_MODE_FALLBACK_DOMINANCE: All live-GPU experiments in this milestone (Exps 340, 347, 346, 341) fell back to simulated mode. Exp 340 had no 'responses' key in its JSON; Exp 347 found no live violation pairs. Both RTX 3090s are confirmed idle (0% util, 4MB VRAM) — the hardware is available but the pipeline from conductor → ExperimentTemplate → model load → live inference is not end-to-end verified for autonomous runs. Simulated fallbacks produce correctly-structured artifacts but zero real GPU provenance.

INCREMENTAL_MILESTONE_PER_EXPERIMENT_REGRESSION: The 21 new experiments in this milestone averaged 20.3 min/exp vs 14.3 min/exp for the prior 378. The regression is not random: complex experiments (EORM transformer Exp 346 = 56 min; two-turn verification Exp 334 = ~24 min) inflate the mean. The milestone batch was intentionally heavy on infrastructure and complex algorithmic work. No alarm, but worth monitoring.

EORM_AND_JEPA_TRAIN_ON_SYNTHETIC_ONLY: Exp 346 (EORM, 56 min) and Exp 347 (JEPA retrain, 17 min) trained on 100% synthetic data because live GPU inference fallback triggered. AUC-ROC of 0.5 for both (random baseline) confirms no signal learned. The training infrastructure is correct but produces no value until live pairs are available. This creates a dependency: live inference must succeed before model learning produces real results.

MULTI_DELIVERABLE_COMPLEXITY_WITHOUT_PRESPLIT: Exp 346 (EORM) required a full JAX transformer implementation, contrastive training loop, safetensors save/load, AUC-ROC evaluation, and full test suite — all in one experiment. Despite existing RETRO guidance to presplit high-complexity experiments into Phase A (implementation + tests) and Phase B (integration + artifact + docs), this was not applied. The 56-minute duration reflects the cost.

DOC_RECONCILIATION_PER_EXPERIMENT_PERSISTS: Changelog, traceability, status.md, and spec reconciliation were still performed after every individual experiment in this milestone. No batching was adopted despite the prior retro recommendation. For 21 experiments this adds moderate overhead; at 378 experiments it was the dominant context-switching cost.
improvements_suggested: ENFORCE_RETRO_003_TIMEOUT_NOW — HIGHEST PRIORITY: Wire run_experiment_with_timeout.sh as the mandatory conductor wrapper before milestone 2026.05.20 begins. Set CARNOT_CONDUCTOR_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=45 (3x current 15-min average). This is the single change with the highest ROI — Exp 53 (418 min) alone justifies it. The tooling already exists; the conductor config change is a one-line environment variable.

CLOSE_RETRO_005_ZOMBIE_KILL: Add gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies (without --dry-run) to the conductor inter-experiment cleanup step. Call it after each experiment artifact is written, before starting the next. Also call it at session startup via session_startup.sh --kill-zombies. The 4MB residual VRAM is growing; auto-kill prevents accumulation.

LIVE_GPU_INFERENCE_INTEGRATION_TEST: Write a single 5-minute smoke test that loads Qwen3.5-0.8B on GPU 0, runs 5 GSM8K questions via BatchedInferenceRunner, and writes a results JSON. Gate every GPU-dependent experiment on this smoke test passing (checked once per session by session_startup.sh). This will prevent all four live-inference experiments from falling back to simulated mode in the next milestone.

PRESPLIT_HIGH_COMPLEXITY_EXPERIMENTS_AT_PLAN_TIME: When writing the milestone plan (research-roadmap-next.yaml), add expected_complexity: high to experiments with >3 deliverables. The conductor should automatically split these into Phase A (implementation + unit tests) and Phase B (integration + artifact + docs). EORM (Exp 346) should have been two separate experiments. Prevents 56-minute single-experiment blocks and reduces max-turn-limit risk.

BATCH_DOC_RECONCILIATION_EVERY_5_EXPERIMENTS: Run changelog, traceability, status.md, and spec reconciliation in a single pass after every 5-experiment batch, not after each individual experiment. Final full reconciliation at milestone end. Reduces context-switching overhead and keeps individual experiment turns focused on implementation.

TRACK_LIVE_VS_SIMULATED_MODE_PER_EXPERIMENT: Add inference_mode: live|simulated|blocked to every experiment artifact at time of writing. The conductor should emit a warning at end-of-milestone if >25% of GPU-tagged experiments ran in simulated mode. This makes silent fallback visible in the milestone summary.

CONDUCTOR_FAIL_FAST_ON_FAILING_TESTS: Extend session_startup.sh's fail-fast behavior to mid-experiment operation: if pytest exits non-zero during an in-progress experiment, the conductor must mark it FAILED (not checkpointed) and pause for human review before proceeding. RETRO-007 closed the pre-session check but Exp 308's pattern (checkpoint with failing tests) can still recur.

ROLLING_AVERAGE_TIMEOUT_RECALCULATION: Update CARNOT_CONDUCTOR_TIMEOUT_MINUTES every 50 experiments using the rolling 50-experiment median. As the codebase matures and experiments get faster, the timeout should tighten. Current 15-min average suggests a 45-min timeout (3x). In 50 experiments, if average drops to 12 min, timeout should auto-adjust to 36 min.

time_distribution_estimate.note: Prereq waste reduced from 3% to ~1% after RETRO-006 (HostPrereqRegistry) closed in Exp 338. estimated_time_savings_rationale: Four of six RETRO items (004, 006, 007, 008) are now closed. These were estimated at ~30% collective savings in the prior retro. RETRO-003 (timeout) and RETRO-005 (zombie kill) remain open, representing ~13% of theoretical savings. With RETRO-003 enforced, Exp 53 alone saves ~375 minutes (~7% of 5392 baseline). DualGPU default (RETRO-004 closed) applies to future experiments. BatchedInferenceRunner default (RETRO-008 closed) applies to future experiments. Live GPU smoke test (new recommendation) enables real inference data, enabling EORM/JEPA to produce meaningful results rather than synthetic-only baselines. Combined: 32% improvement estimate for next milestone, slightly below the prior retro's 38% prediction because RETRO-003 was not closed as planned. If RETRO-003 is closed before 2026.05.20, the savings should reach 35-40%.
estimated_next_milestone_rationale: 5818 minutes baseline × (1 - 0.32) ≈ 3955 minutes for the same experiment count. If Exp 53 is excluded from the baseline (as it would be under a timeout regime), the calculation is (5818 - 375) × (1 - 0.25) ≈ 4085 minutes — comparable. The 32% estimate is conservative; if live GPU inference is successfully unlocked, EORM/JEPA experiments will generate real learning signal and may complete faster per experiment.

meta_reflection: Milestone 2026.05.13 closed 4 of 6 carry-forward RETRO items from the prior milestone — a good closure rate. The 21 new experiments averaged 20.3 min/exp, a 42% regression vs the prior 14.3 min/exp baseline. This regression is explainable: the milestone was deliberately front-loaded with infrastructure (Exp 338, 339) and high-complexity algorithmic work (Exp 346 EORM at 56 min). The more concerning finding is that RETRO-003 (timeout guard) was not closed for the second consecutive milestone. The tooling exists in run_experiment_with_timeout.sh; the conductor config change has been recommended twice. This represents a process failure: a known high-ROI improvement is being repeatedly deferred. A rule for the next milestone: RETRO items that survive two consecutive milestones must be addressed in the first experiment of the following milestone, before any new work begins. The second structural finding is that all four live GPU experiments fell back to simulated mode — the hardware is available and idle, but the inference pipeline from conductor to model is not autonomously verified at session start. RETRO-009 (live GPU smoke test) is the fix. Both findings share a pattern: the infrastructure to solve the problem exists, but it is not wired into the automated path. The next milestone's first priority should be closing the gap between 'tooling exists' and 'tooling runs automatically.'
